title: Assessing vertebrate physiology: A simple and cost-effective method to exercise adult zebrafish.
author: Sven Reischauer
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.sa2eage
materials: Difficult to determine precise water speed.
5L glass or plastic beaker (e.g. Schott Duran)
adjustable tabletop magnetic stirrer (e.g. VWR VMS-C7)
Replace water with fresh system water
Continue the same procedure in following days.

steps.title: Prepare fish and beaker
steps.instruction: Select adult zebrafish that are at least 12 mm in length (approximately 2.5–3 months post‑fertilization). If using mutant lines, confirm that they swim normally and can learn circular currents. Place a 5 L beaker on top of a magnetic stirrer.

steps.title: Add water and stir bar
steps.instruction: Put a magnetic stir bar into the beaker and add 4 L of system water.

steps.title: Generate low‑speed vortex
steps.instruction: Switch on the stirrer to create a slow water current that produces a vertical vortex in the centre of the beaker. Adjust the speed so the vortex diameter is ≤1 cm and the rotation remains gentle.

steps.title: Introduce fish and start learning
steps.instruction: Turn off the stirrer, gently place up to 10 fish (recommended cohort size n + 2) into the beaker, then switch the stirrer back on at low speed. Allow the fish to adjust and learn to avoid the central vortex; the speed must be sufficient to require active avoidance but not so high that fish become permanently trapped.

steps.title: Gradual speed increase – first session
steps.instruction: After 1 hour, slightly increase the water speed while confirming that no fish are trapped in the vortex. Continue to raise the speed slowly over the next 3–4 hours, constantly monitoring for trapped fish. The total training time for this session may be up to 5 hours.

steps.title: Rest and feeding
steps.instruction: Stop the stirrer and let the fish rest for 1 hour. Fish may be fed during this period; ensure the amount of food matches that given to the non‑exercised control cohort.

steps.title: Remove non‑learning individuals
steps.instruction: If any single fish continuously become trapped in the vortex and fail to learn, remove that fish from the cohort to avoid slowing the setup for the others.

steps.title: Extended training and overnight storage
steps.instruction: Optionally continue to increase the water speed slowly for an additional up to 5 hours of training. Then stop the current and return the fish to the main fish system for overnight housing. Clean the beaker and store the setup.

steps.title: Next‑day exercise – setup
steps.instruction: Place a clean 5 L beaker on the magnetic stirrer, add a stir bar and 4 L of system water, and transfer the fish back into the beaker.

steps.title: Resume stirring at previous speed
steps.instruction: Start the stirrer at the same speed used at the end of the previous evening. Verify that no fish are trapped and run the stirrer for 1 hour.

steps.title: Increase speed to maximal desired
steps.instruction: Over the next 4 hours, gradually increase the water current until the maximal desired speed for the experiment is reached.

steps.title: Midday rest and feeding
steps.instruction: Allow the fish to rest for 1 hour around noon. Feed them, matching the amount given to the control cohort.

steps.title: Final exercise escalation
steps.instruction: Continue increasing water speed until the maximal experimental speed is achieved (e.g., for sprint or interval tasks). Remove any fish that still fail to avoid the vortex, as described earlier.

steps.title: Final training and overnight storage
steps.instruction: After an additional up to 5 hours of training, stop the current and return the fish to the main fish system for overnight storage. Clean the beaker.

steps.title: Tissue collection
steps.instruction: After completing the exercise protocol (or after a defined recovery period), harvest organs or tissues from the exercised and control cohorts at any desired stage for downstream analyses.
